Heat.question: In a vacuum flask, what is the main purpose of the silvered walls facing the vacuum?

options.B: Reduce heat transfer by convection
options.D: Increase the heat capacity of the flask

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: C. A/B confuse vacuum’s role (stops conduction/convection) with silvering (reflects IR). D invents a capacity change.

Heat.question: For an ideal gas kept at constant temperature, a graph of pressure p against 1/V is

options.B: a straight line through the origin
options.C: a straight line with negative gradient

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: B. Boyle: p ∝ 1/V. A is what students draw for p–V. C mixes Charles/Gay-Lussac shapes.

Heat.question: The pressure of an ideal gas on the walls of a container is mainly due to

options.B: collisions of molecules with the walls

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: B. A is the classic misconception flagged in reports. C/D not kinetic-theory pressure.

Heat.question: When using pV = nRT, temperature must be in

options.B: kelvin

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: B. Students plug °C (HEAT_GASES-06). Absolute thermodynamic T required.

Heat.question: Two objects of equal mass but different specific heat capacities start at different temperatures and reach thermal equilibrium. The final temperature is

options.A: always the arithmetic mean of the two initial temperatures
options.B: closer to the initial T of the object with larger heat capacity mc
options.C: closer to the initial T of the object with smaller c

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: B. Equal mass ≠ equal share of ΔT. Q = mcΔT → larger C means smaller |ΔT|.

Heat.question: A good thermal conductor (e.g. copper) compared with a poor conductor of the same mass and same ΔT

options.B: always absorbs less thermal energy
options.C: may absorb the same energy if heat capacities are equal; conduction describes rate/path, not stored Q

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: C. 2021 misconception: conductor ≠ larger heat capacity. Conduction ≠ capacity.

Heat.question: In the equation pV = nRT, n stands for

options.B: number of moles

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: B. HEAT_GASES-10: moles vs molecules confusion (2025).

Heat.question: Which statement about latent heat is correct?

options.A: During melting at the melting point, temperature rises steadily as latent heat is absorbed
options.B: Latent heat of vaporization is energy per unit mass to change liquid↔vapour at constant T
options.C: Latent heat only applies to water
options.D: Latent heat equals mcΔT for any process

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: B. A confuses sensible vs latent. D mixes formulas.

Heat.question: Internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on

options.B: volume alone
options.D: how the gas was compressed historically

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: C. State function for ideal gas U(T). Path myths common.

Heat.question: In a vacuum flask, the vacuum between walls mainly reduces heat transfer by

options.B: conduction and convection

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: B. Pair with Q1: silver→radiation; vacuum→conduction/convection.

Heat.question: Absolute zero on the kelvin scale is the temperature at which

options.B: an ideal gas would have zero volume/pressure extrapolating from Charles’s law behaviour
options.C: all real molecular motion in every material has been proven to stop completely for all substances
options.D: Celsius and kelvin readings are equal

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live bank has absolute-zero wording; refine fact: thermodynamic/ideal-gas definition vs overclaim C.

Heat.question: Heat capacity C of an object is

options.A: energy to raise temperature by 1 K (for that object)
options.B: energy per kg per K
options.D: always equal to mc with c of water

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: A. c = specific; C = object. Conductivity ≠ capacity (links HEAT_GASES-08).

Heat.question: On a sunny day a dark car roof feels hotter than a light roof mainly because the dark surface

options.B: absorbs more thermal radiation

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: B. Kirchhoff/radiation fact; D false (good absorbers are good emitters).

Heat.question: When compressed gas is pumped into a structure at the seabed, its pressure must be

options.B: greater than the surrounding water pressure at that depth
options.C: less than water pressure so water can push it in

Heat.question: Relation between pressure, force and area is

options.B: p = F / A

Heat.question: During boiling of pure water at constant pressure, adding heat mainly

options.B: increases average KE of liquid molecules without phase change
options.C: provides latent heat to convert liquid to vapour at constant T

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: C. Latent vs sensible fact.

Heat.question: Charles’s law (constant p) relates volume and temperature. Temperature must be measured from

options.B: an absolute (kelvin) scale for the linear V ∝ T form through origin
options.D: the ice point as zero with V ∝ t(°C) through origin

Heat.explanation: Correct answer: B. V–T through origin only on absolute scale.

Force.question: A book rests on a table. The book’s weight and the table’s normal reaction

options.B: are equal and opposite forces on the same body (equilibrium pair, not N3)
options.D: only balance if the table is accelerating

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. Classic N3 trap (2021). N3 pair: Earth–book gravity and book–Earth.

Force.question: Newton’s third-law action and reaction forces always

options.A: act on the same object and cancel
options.B: act on different objects
options.C: have different magnitudes if masses differ

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_FORCES-03.

Force.question: A block slides down a rough incline at constant velocity. The net force along the slope is

options.B: zero

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. Constant v ⇒ ΣF = 0 (N1).

Force.question: On a v–t graph, two cars’ traces cross. At that instant they necessarily have the same

options.B: velocity

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. Intersection = same v; same position needs equal areas.

Force.question: In uniform circular motion, ‘the centripetal force’ is best described as

options.A: a new type of force in addition to weight and tension/friction
options.B: the name for the net force toward the centre provided by real forces
options.D: always equal to friction alone, by definition

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_FORCES-14: labelling friction/weight ‘as’ centripetal.

Force.question: A spring balance measures

options.B: force (often calibrated as weight reading)
options.C: mass in all situations including free fall without caveat

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_FORCES-12: reading given in metres.

Force.question: In a freely falling lift (ideal free fall), a beam balance comparing two masses

options.A: reads slightly less than true mass ratio
options.B: reads slightly more
options.C: cannot give the usual ‘weight comparison’ reading because both sides are weightless effectively

Force.explanation: Correct answer: C. MECH_FORCES-18: not merely ‘decreases’.

Force.question: If forces on a body are balanced (net force zero), the body

options.B: must have zero acceleration (rest or uniform velocity)

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live Mech T/F + MECH_FORCES-10 contradiction myth.

Force.question: For a rocket going straight up, net force is best written as

options.B: thrust + weight

Force.explanation: Correct answer: C. MECH_FORCES-11.

Force.question: A projectile in flight (ignore air). At the highest point

options.B: velocity is zero
options.C: vertical velocity component is zero; horizontal may be non-zero so KE ≠ 0

Force.explanation: Correct answer: C. MECH_ENERGY-07 (>50% miss).

Force.question: Weight and air resistance on a falling projectile

options.B: both act on the projectile so cannot be a Newton III pair

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_FORCES-09.

Force.question: Kinetic friction on a sliding block

options.A: becomes zero the instant an applied push is removed, even if still sliding
options.B: acts while there is sliding, opposing relative motion
options.C: always equals μN with N = mg on every incline with extra forces
options.D: acts in the direction of velocity

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_FORCES-05.

Force.question: On a free-body diagram for a block on an incline, you should

options.A: draw weight, normal, friction (as needed) — not also ‘mg sinθ’ and ‘resultant’ as extra force arrows on top of mg
options.B: always draw mg sinθ as a separate force in addition to full weight
options.D: draw centripetal force even for straight incline motion

Force.explanation: Correct answer: A. MECH_FORCES-13 double-counting.

Force.question: Change in velocity is a

options.B: vector; magnitude by vector subtraction, not |v₂|−|v₁| alone when direction changes

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_FORCES-08 east→north example.

Force.question: When a bungee cord first becomes taut

options.A: the jumper must start decelerating immediately
options.B: net force may still be downward if weight > cord force, so downward speed can still increase for a while

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_FORCES-17.

Force.question: Area under a force–time graph equals

options.B: impulse (Δp)

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_ENERGY-06; fact units.

Force.question: Area under a force–displacement graph equals

options.B: work done

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. Pair with previous.

Force.question: A car headrest’s main safety role in a rear-end collision is to

options.A: reduce injury mainly when braking hard from the front
options.B: support the head to reduce whiplash as the seat pushes the torso forward

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_ENERGY-05.

Force.question: On a smooth incline, two paths same height: final speeds from rest (energy)

options.B: same (same loss of PE → same KE if smooth)

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_ENERGY-01; time differs (ENERGY-02).

Force.question: For circular motion of a whirling bob on a string, tension

options.A: equals weight + ‘centripetal force’ treated as an extra force object
options.B: is one of the real forces; net of tension (and weight components) toward centre is mv²/r
options.C: is always equal to mv²/r with weight ignored in all geometries

Force.explanation: Correct answer: B. MECH_FORCES-15.

Wave.question: When a water wave travels from shallow to deep water, its frequency

options.B: decreases

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: C. WAVES-07.

Wave.question: When light enters glass from air, its frequency

options.B: decreases

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: C. WAVES-08 · live T/F.

Wave.question: On a stretched string, if frequency doubles while tension and mass/length fixed, wave speed

options.B: halves

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: C. WAVES-01: v not ∝ f on same string.

Wave.question: In a longitudinal sound wave, a particle at the equilibrium position

options.B: may have maximum speed there (like SHM through centre)
options.C: only moves perpendicular to wave travel

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES-02.

Wave.question: Particle motion in a longitudinal wave is

options.B: parallel to propagation

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES-03 (~half wrong direction).

Wave.question: Two waves of different frequencies at one point

options.A: always reinforce to a larger fixed amplitude
options.B: do not form a steady interference maximum like equal-f coherent sources

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES-04.

Wave.question: Stable interference fringes from two sources require the sources to be

options.B: coherent (constant phase relation)

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES-05: incoherent ≠ merely ‘out of phase’.

Wave.question: Microwaves in air travel at approximately

options.B: speed of light

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES-10.

Wave.question: An echo sounding measures depth using travel time t. Distance is proportional to

options.B: ½ vt (there and back)

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES-09.

Wave.question: Apparent depth of a pool floor viewed from air is

options.B: shallower than real

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES_OPTICS-01 · live T/F.

Wave.question: A short-sighted (myopic) person cannot see distant objects clearly. Correction uses a

options.B: concave (diverging) lens

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES_OPTICS-02.

Wave.question: A ray in denser medium meets a boundary with air. If it refracts into air, it bends

options.B: away from the normal

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES_OPTICS-05.

Wave.question: Diffraction and refraction are

options.A: the same effect with different names
options.B: different: refraction = speed/direction change across media; diffraction = spreading at obstacles/apertures

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES_OPTICS-07.

Wave.question: EM spectrum: which travels at c in vacuum?

options.B: only radio

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: C. Fact order/speed.

Wave.question: Constructive interference of two coherent waves of equal amplitude occurs when path difference is

options.B: nλ
options.C: always zero only if amplitudes differ

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live Waves T/F crest–trough myth inverse.

Wave.question: For ultrasound imaging of fine detail, higher frequency generally gives

options.A: worse resolution but is chosen because ‘less harmful’
options.B: better resolution (shorter λ), with penetration trade-offs

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. WAVES-11.

Wave.question: Polarisation is a property that demonstrates

options.B: light (EM) has transverse character

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. Fact: longitudinal sound not polarised.

Wave.question: In Young’s double slit, increasing slit separation a (other things fixed) makes fringe spacing

options.B: smaller

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. Δy = λD/a. Distinct from coherence failure (WAVES-06).

Wave.question: Amplitude of a mechanical wave is most directly related to

options.B: energy/intensity carried
options.C: wave speed in the medium only

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live Waves T/F.

Wave.question: Critical angle for glass→air depends on

options.A: only the refractive index of glass relative to air (and geometry definition)
options.B: the colour of the observer’s shirt

Wave.explanation: Correct answer: A. Refine vs WAVES_OPTICS-06 layered water/glass trap: know which indices enter sin c = 1/n.

E&M.question: A metal rod moves in a magnetic field but is not part of a closed circuit. There can be

options.A: an induced current along the rod anyway
options.B: an induced e.m.f. (charge separation) but no sustained current
options.C: neither e.m.f. nor any charge shift

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-02 (>30%).

E&M.question: Magnetic force on a current-carrying wire is

options.B: perpendicular to B (and to I) when F = BIL sinθ

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-03.

E&M.question: Open conducting rod moving in B: opposing magnetic drag force

options.B: requires induced current; without closed path, no magnetic drag of that kind
options.D: is electrostatic only and always huge

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-09 (>40%).

E&M.question: When magnetic flux through a rotating coil is instantaneously zero, induced e.m.f./current is

options.B: often maximum because dΦ/dt is largest then

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-12 Faraday: e.m.f. ∝ rate of change.

E&M.question: Eddy-current braking on a vehicle

options.A: works even when the vehicle is completely at rest
options.B: needs relative motion / changing flux while moving

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-15.

E&M.question: After the field of a coil becomes steady, eddy currents in a nearby metal ring

options.B: stop (no changing flux) so magnetic lift/force from eddy effects ceases

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-18.

E&M.question: Unlike magnetic poles

options.B: attract

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-14 unlike attract; not ± charge.

E&M.question: Raising resistance of a heater on fixed mains voltage

options.A: increases power (P = V²/R falls when R rises)
options.B: decreases power for fixed V

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-11 (~40% thought power rises).

E&M.question: Mains ‘220 V’ in HK normally means

options.B: r.m.s. voltage

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-19.

E&M.question: Electric shock hazard is primarily due to

options.A: high voltage by itself with zero current
options.B: large current through the body
options.D: colour of the wire insulation only

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-21.

E&M.question: A bird can perch on a single high-voltage bare cable mainly because

options.A: the cable is always thickly insulated
options.B: both feet are at nearly the same potential so little current through the bird
options.D: voltage is zero on all cables

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-20 insulation myth.

E&M.question: In a simple d.c. motor, current in the armature coil

options.A: keeps one direction all the time without commutation
options.B: is reversed each half-turn by the commutator so torque direction stays useful

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-06.

E&M.question: Charged particle moving in uniform B (F magnetic only)

options.B: speed stays the same; direction can change (circular/helical)

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-13 (~30%).

E&M.question: Electron moving parallel to B experiences magnetic force

options.B: zero (sinθ = 0)

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live E&M T/F.

E&M.question: Lamps dark in a circuit may be

options.B: open OR shorted (bypassed) — need to diagnose

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-22 short vs open.

E&M.question: Adding identical resistors in parallel

options.B: decreases total resistance

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live E&M T/F.

E&M.question: Transformer action requires

options.B: changing flux (usually a.c.) linking coils

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live ‘transformer can’t step up DC’.

E&M.question: Electric field direction is the direction of force on a

options.B: positive test charge

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. Potential decreases along field lines (live T/F related).

E&M.question: Resistance R of a uniform wire satisfies

options.B: R ∝ ℓ / A

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-08 cube face trap: don’t forget length.

E&M.question: In parallel branches, energy transferred per unit charge through each branch (from same two nodes) is

options.A: larger in the brighter lamp only because brightness means higher V
options.B: the same (same pd); brightness differences come from current/power

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. ELEC-05 energy per coulomb = V.

E&M.question: Lenz’s law: induced current direction

options.B: opposes the change in flux that produces it
options.D: is always from N to S outside magnets only

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live T/F + Faraday cluster (E&M lowest avgs 2022 **42%**, 2023 **47%**).

E&M.question: Magnetic field along the axis inside a long solenoid is

options.A: strongest at the ends and zero in middle
options.B: approximately uniform and strong inside, weaker outside

E&M.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live E&M T/F ends myth.

options.A: always a spontaneous process like α decay
options.B: not generally spontaneous; needs extreme conditions to overcome repulsion
options.C: the splitting of a heavy nucleus

Radiation.question: A film badge worn in air is generally unsuitable for monitoring α exposure because

options.B: α have very short range in air and usually don’t reach the badge
options.C: α are undetectable by any film

Radiation.explanation: Correct answer: B. RAD-02 (~⅓ accounted for range).

Radiation.question: Isotopes of an element have

options.A: same mass number, different atomic number
options.B: same atomic number Z, different mass number A (different N)
options.D: different Z and different chemical behaviour always as different elements

Radiation.explanation: Correct answer: B. RAD-10 · live T/F opposite wording.

Radiation.question: Binding energy of a nucleus is

options.A: energy you must supply to assemble nucleons into the nucleus
options.B: energy required to separate the nucleus into individual nucleons
options.C: always equal to mc² of one electron
options.D: the kinetic energy of α particles only

Radiation.question: Moderator in a thermal fission reactor slows

options.B: neutrons
options.C: α particles in fuel rods as primary purpose

Radiation.question: Most α particles pass straight through thin gold foil. This observation alone

options.A: is enough to rule out Thomson’s plum-pudding model
options.B: fits both plum-pudding and nuclear models, so does not by itself invalidate Thomson

Radiation.question: γ radiation in a magnetic field is

options.B: undeflected (uncharged EM radiation)

Radiation.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live Atomic T/F.

Radiation.question: A pure radioisotope that appears to emit α, β and γ may do so because

options.A: the sample must be chemically impure
options.B: a decay series / daughter products contribute different radiations

options.A: activity is automatically negligible and always harmless regardless of quantity
options.B: decay is slow per nucleus; hazard still depends on amount, type, and exposure

Radiation.question: Nuclear fission is

options.B: splitting a heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei

Radiation.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live T/F opposite.

Radiation.question: α particles ‘neutralise’ charged smoke/dust in a detector mainly by

options.A: chemically combining with dust particles directly as the whole story
options.B: ionising air; ions then neutralise charged particles

Radiation.question: Half-life is the time for

options.B: half the nuclei (of a large sample) to decay

Radiation.explanation: Correct answer: B. Live T/F definition.

Radiation.question: Power delivered by a radioisotope heat source depends most directly on

options.A: total number of atoms ignoring decay rate
options.B: activity (decays per second) and energy per decay

Radiation.question: If moderator water is lost in a thermal reactor, the chain reaction may stop because

options.B: supply of slowed neutrons for fission is lost
options.C: neutrons become too slow to do anything ever

Radiation.question: α, β, γ ionising ability / penetrating power (qualitative)

options.B: α least penetrating (stopped by paper/few cm air); γ most penetrating of the three

Radiation.explanation: Correct answer: B. Core fact weak memorisation.

Radiation.question: Energy invested in pushing two nuclei together against electrostatic repulsion is stored mainly as

options.A: random heat only with no potential
options.B: electrical potential energy
options.C: nuclear binding already more negative automatically

Energy and Use of Energy.question: The kilowatt-hour (kW·h) is a unit of

options.B: energy

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: B. Power is in W or kW; energy = power × time, so kW·h is energy (MECH_ENERGY-19).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: A domestic appliance rated 2 kW runs for 3 hours. Energy transferred from the mains is closest to

options.B: 6 kW

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: A. E = Pt = 2 kW × 3 h = 6 kW·h. A confuses energy with power.

Energy and Use of Energy.question: Electricity tariff charges are usually based mainly on

options.B: resistance of wiring only

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: C. Domestic cost tracks energy consumed (and sometimes demand), not voltage or frequency alone.

Energy and Use of Energy.question: Regenerative braking on a vehicle mainly recovers energy by

options.A: converting kinetic energy of the vehicle into electrical energy to recharge a battery
options.B: storing heat from friction pads as electrical energy
options.D: turning gravitational PE of the road into chemical energy in petrol

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: A. Common myth: that friction-heat is what gets stored (MECH_ENERGY-13).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: If a regenerative-braking battery is already full, the vehicle

options.B: must accelerate until the battery empties
options.D: can still be stopped using ordinary friction brakes (regen may be limited)

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: D. Battery state does not remove friction braking (MECH_ENERGY-14).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: On a level road at steady speed against constant drag, a heavier vehicle compared with a lighter one

options.A: always needs much larger driving force just to keep that same steady speed
options.B: needs zero power
options.C: does not need extra driving force merely because of mass; extra force/power matters mainly when accelerating

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: C. Steady speed: drive force balances drag. Mass enters acceleration (MECH_ENERGY-15).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: Power and work done are

options.A: different: power is the rate of doing work / transferring energy
options.B: the same physical quantity

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: A. Students confuse P with W when using P = Fv (MECH_ENERGY-16).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: Lamp luminous efficacy and electrical efficiency are

options.A: always identical names for the same ratio
options.B: both measured only in ohms
options.D: related ideas but not the same: efficacy concerns useful light per electrical power; efficiency is broader energy conversion

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: D. Efficiency ≠ efficacy mix-up (GENERAL-13 / Paper 2 energy).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: Painting a photovoltaic solar cell’s active surface black

options.A: must raise electrical energy output because black absorbs more radiation
options.B: makes efficiency automatically 100%
options.C: need not raise electrical output: absorption as heat is not the same as photovoltaic conversion
options.D: turns sunlight into chemical energy in silicon always

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: C. Black ≠ more electricity (HEAT_GASES-12 / renewable).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: In a simple solar–battery setup, useful bookkeeping of energy forms should include that

options.A: solar input is electromagnetic radiation; the battery stores chemical energy when charged
options.B: the Sun’s thermal energy is converted directly to electricity and the battery’s chemical store can be ignored

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: A. Wrong chain: “thermal→electrical” and omitting battery chemical energy (GENERAL-14).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: A building material with a larger U-value (other things equal) means

options.A: better insulation (less heat loss rate per area per temperature difference)
options.B: higher electrical resistivity
options.D: poorer insulation: higher thermal transmittance / faster heat loss for given ΔT and area

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: D. U-value = heat transfer rate per unit area per unit temperature difference — higher U ⇒ worse insulator (Energy: building performance).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: Double glazing reduces heat loss through a window mainly by

options.B: trapping a poorly conducting gas/air layer so conduction/convection across the pane gap falls

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: B. Insulation qualitative: trapped air / gap cuts conduction–convection (Energy: buildings).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: Which is a renewable energy source in the usual DSE classification sense?

options.B: natural gas

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: C. Wind is renewable; coal/gas/oil are non-renewable fossil fuels.

Energy and Use of Energy.question: Fossil fuels are classed as non-renewable mainly because

options.A: they release no energy when burned
options.B: they form far more slowly than we use them
options.D: they have infinite reserves on human timescales

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: B. Formation rate ≪ consumption rate (renewable vs non-renewable).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: For the same useful output, a process with higher efficiency

options.A: wastes a smaller fraction of input energy
options.B: wastes a larger fraction of input energy
options.D: has efficiency above 100% in a heat engine

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: A. η = useful output / input; higher η ⇒ less waste fraction.

Energy and Use of Energy.question: In a pressurised-water reactor (PWR), the pressurised primary coolant water typically

options.A: boils and that steam directly drives the turbine
options.B: is only a moderator and carries no heat
options.C: stays liquid under high pressure; heat is transferred to a secondary loop that produces steam for the turbine

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: C. Primary stays liquid; secondary makes steam (RAD-09 / Paper 2 Energy).

Energy and Use of Energy.question: Using LED lighting instead of an inefficient lamp for the same useful light generally

options.A: increases electrical energy use for that lighting task
options.B: changes the mains frequency
options.C: removes the need for any power source
options.D: reduces electrical energy use because more of the input becomes useful light (less waste heat per lumen)

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: D. Lighting / saving energy: higher efficacy → less electrical energy for same light.

Energy and Use of Energy.question: Transport energy efficiency discussions often emphasise that regenerative braking

options.A: replaces the need for any friction brakes forever
options.B: can return some kinetic energy to stored electrical energy, improving overall energy use on stop–go journeys
options.C: increases fuel use at every stop
options.D: only works on vehicles with empty fuel tanks

Energy and Use of Energy.explanation: Correct answer: B. Ties MECH_ENERGY-13/14 to transport efficiency (Paper 2 Energy).

Atomic World.question: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of light (same frequency above threshold) mainly increases

options.A: the maximum kinetic energy of each photoelectron
options.B: the work function of the metal
options.C: the number of photoelectrons emitted per second (photocurrent), not Kmax
options.D: the threshold frequency of the metal

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: C. Intensity → more photons → more electrons; Kmax set by frequency (ATOMIC-06).

Atomic World.question: Increasing the frequency of incident light above threshold (intensity fixed) mainly

options.A: increases maximum photoelectron KE; saturation current is not set by frequency
options.B: increases saturation photocurrent in proportion to frequency

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: A. Frequency↔Kmax; saturation current↔intensity (ATOMIC-01).

Atomic World.question: Stopping potential Vs in a photoelectric experiment satisfies

options.A: Vs equals Kmax numerically in joules with no conversion
options.B: eVs = Kmax
options.C: Vs equals the work function in eV always
options.D: Vs equals photon energy hf with no subtraction of work function

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: B. Students conflate Vs, Kmax and work function (ATOMIC-02/03).

Atomic World.question: The work function of a metal is

options.A: equal to hf for any incident light used
options.B: the same as stopping potential in volts with no e factor
options.D: the minimum energy needed to free an electron from the surface; not simply “the photon energy” of whatever light is shining

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: D. Taking hf as φ is a common slip (ATOMIC-04).

Atomic World.question: Photoelectrons from a metal illuminated by monochromatic light show a spread of KE mainly because

options.A: electrons inside the metal need different energies to reach the surface (work function is a minimum); emission itself sets the spread
options.B: electrons lose random amounts of energy only while drifting from cathode to anode in the tube
options.C: the photon energy changes after each collision with air
options.D: magnetic fields in the lab quantise KE

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: A. Spread is about emission / φ, not flight to anode (ATOMIC-05).

Atomic World.question: The threshold frequency of a metal

options.A: rises whenever you use a higher-frequency lamp
options.B: is the same for all metals
options.C: is a property of the metal (linked to work function), not something that tracks the lamp frequency you happen to choose

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: C. Mixing threshold with incident frequency (ATOMIC-07).

Atomic World.question: In photoelectric equations, c in E = hc/λ is

options.B: the speed of light in vacuum (photon), not the electron’s speed

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: B. Confusing photon E,c with electron KE,v (ATOMIC-08).

Atomic World.question: In the Bohr model of hydrogen, while the electron remains in an allowed orbit it

options.A: continuously radiates EM waves like a classical accelerating charge
options.B: must spiral into the nucleus in microseconds
options.D: does not radiate; energy of that stationary state stays constant until a jump

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: D. Non-classical: no radiation in allowed orbit (ATOMIC_BOHR-01).

Atomic World.question: A photon can excite a hydrogen atom from one Bohr level to a higher one only if

options.A: its energy matches the exact level difference ΔE (one photon ↔ one transition)
options.B: its energy is any value larger than the level gap ΔE
options.D: the photon energy equals the electron’s total energy at the upper level alone

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: A. Exact ΔE match; photons don’t “pool” (ATOMIC_BOHR-02/04). Also ATOMIC-09: level energy ≠ photon energy of transition.

Atomic World.question: The first excited state of hydrogen corresponds to
Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: B. Ground state n=1; 1st excited n=2 (ATOMIC_BOHR-03).

Atomic World.question: Bohr orbit radius scales as rn ∝ n². Compared with the ground-state radius, the first excited orbit is

options.B: 2 times larger

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: C. n=2 ⇒ r2 = 4 r1 (ATOMIC_BOHR-07).

Atomic World.question: Excitation of an atom and ionisation of an atom are

options.B: both impossible for hydrogen
options.D: different: excitation raises an electron to a higher bound level; ionisation removes it from the atom

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: D. Excitation ≠ ionisation (ATOMIC-10).

Atomic World.question: To ionise ground-state hydrogen, a photon must have

options.A: energy at least 13.6 eV; excess can appear as KE of the freed electron
options.B: energy exactly 13.6 eV only; any larger energy cannot ionise
options.D: energy equal to the Rydberg gas constant in joules

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: A. ≥ ionisation energy works (ATOMIC_BOHR-05). Rydberg ≠ gas constant (ATOMIC-11).

Atomic World.question: If a photon’s energy exceeds the ionisation energy of an atom,

options.A: the atom absorbs only part of the photon and the same photon continues with the leftover energy
options.B: photons never interact with atoms
options.C: the atom can absorb the whole photon; ionisation occurs and excess energy can go to the electron’s KE
options.D: only elastic scattering of half the energy is allowed

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: C. Quantum: whole photon absorbed (ATOMIC-12).

Atomic World.question: In Rutherford’s nuclear model, electrons

options.A: must fall straight into the nucleus because attraction has no orbit idea
options.B: are outside a tiny nucleus; classical orbits still had a radiation problem that Bohr later addressed
options.C: fill the entire atom uniformly like plum pudding
options.D: are inside the nucleus with the protons

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: B. “Falls in with no orbit” misconception (ATOMIC-13).

Atomic World.question: Most α particles pass straight through thin gold foil. By itself this observation

options.B: proves neutrons exist
options.C: proves electrons orbit in Bohr radii
options.D: fits both plum-pudding and nuclear models, so it alone does not rule out Thomson

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: D. Straight-through alone doesn’t kill Thomson (RAD-08); large-angle scatters do.

Atomic World.question: A nanoparticle of a material

options.A: need not have a different shape; nano refers to size scale, not a mandatory shape change
options.B: must always have a different shape from the same material in bulk
options.D: must be exactly one atom across

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: A. Shape-must-differ myth (ATOMIC-14).

Atomic World.question: Resolving power and minimum angular separation: a higher resolving power corresponds to

options.B: infinite wavelength only

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: C. Smaller θmin ⇒ better resolving power (ATOMIC-15).

Atomic World.question: The energy of a photon emitted in a hydrogen transition equals

options.A: the electron’s total energy in the upper level alone
options.B: the difference between the two level energies involved
options.D: the Rydberg constant numerically in eV with no formula

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: B. Photon energy = |ΔE| between levels, not E_n of one level (ATOMIC-09).

Atomic World.question: Light’s wave–particle behaviour is illustrated by the fact that

options.A: interference needs waves while the photoelectric effect needs quantised photons — both can be true of light
options.B: light is only a wave forever
options.C: light is only a particle forever
options.D: photoelectric effect proves light has no frequency

Atomic World.explanation: Correct answer: A. Wave–particle duality: interference vs photoelectric (live Atomic T/F theme).
